title: createRequestHandler
summary: Create Node/Express middleware for SSR documents and loader/action HTTP requests.

sections.title: Options
sections.body: build exports default(request, entry) and handleDataRequest(request), each returning a Response or Promise<Response>. entry is the deployed browser entry URL from the Vite manifest. See the Express and Node hosting guide for a complete server.
sections.code:
import { createRequestHandler } from "@kasperrt/smolter/utils/http";

app.use(createRequestHandler({ build, entry: "/assets/client.js" }));

sections.title: Middleware order
sections.body: Mount Prometheus, tracing, authentication, body size limits and static serving first. Leave request bodies as raw bytes. The adapter returns 400 if earlier middleware calls setEncoding() on an upload. Mount body parsers on separate routes. Genuine render and stream failures are passed to next(error). Clean client disconnects cancel the response without calling error middleware. Express trust proxy remains your application’s responsibility. The adapter does not start a server, install Prometheus, or depend on Express.

sections.title: Returns
sections.body: Route data uses the reserved .__smolter suffix. /users.__smolter?page=2 dispatches /users?page=2; /users/.__smolter preserves the trailing slash. Document requests call build.default. Explicit dataEndpoint retains legacy ?url= transport. Invalid targets, backslash or protocol-relative paths, non-http schemes, and Host headers that are malformed or normalize to a different name return 400. Data responses use private, no-store. When build.default renders personalized HTML itself, set Cache-Control: private, no-store on that Response. Apply authorization inside loaders/actions or match both the route path and its .__smolter suffix (Express app.use("/admin", ...) does not match /admin.__smolter). Reserve the suffix in Express/static middleware. Client disconnection aborts the Request; responses stream with backpressure and preserve existing Set-Cookie headers.

sections.title: Early shell interactivity
sections.body: Configure earlyHydration on renderApplication in your server entry, not on this middleware. Keep reverse-proxy buffering disabled if the shell must arrive before optional data. The adapter respects response backpressure and flushes compression when the response provides flush(). A disconnected browser aborts the request and cancels its response reader. Responses returned after disconnection are cancelled instead of piped to a closed socket.

sections.title: Request security
sections.body: Since 0.5.2, mutations accept POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE only. Other unsafe methods return 405 before actions run. An Origin must exactly match the request URL origin; opaque or foreign origins and Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site return 403. Headerless server clients remain supported. Route-data and rendered SSR responses enforce private/no-store caching, including existing targeted CDN Cache-Control and Surrogate-Control headers. This includes thrown data Responses, inherited Node response cache headers, and page redirects. Resource-only document routes retain their explicit caching contract. CDN configuration must respect origin policy. Authentication, authorization and CSRF tokens remain application responsibilities. Behind a reverse proxy, construct the Request with the public URL or configure Express protocol/trust proxy for your trusted proxy only. Smolter does not trust forwarded headers automatically. The scheme must be http or https, and a Host header must already be the parsed host: percent-encoding, non-ASCII characters, and aliases such as a hexadecimal address return 400. Backslash and protocol-relative targets do too. Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding from the handler are not copied onto the Node response. The Node and Vite adapters cap request bodies at 1 MiB by default; configure maxBodySize for larger uploads. Direct Web Request integrations must enforce their own byte limit. Keep request-time, rate and concurrency limits in the hosting layer; do not consume the stream with a body parser.

sections.title: Request body limit (0.5.2)
sections.body: Node createRequestHandler and Vite applicationPlugins/routerPlugin default to maxBodySize: 1048576 (1 MiB). Oversized declared lengths are rejected before reading; chunked bodies are counted as received and return 413 before application handlers run. The limit includes multipart overhead and counts received bytes, not decompressed content. Configure the same finite, nonnegative integer in production and development for intentionally larger uploads; zero permits only empty bodies. Keep hosting timeouts, rate/concurrency limits and any decompression limits. Low-level webRequest accepts this limit as its fourth argument and throws a Response for policy or size rejection; the provided middleware sends it automatically.

sections.title: Custom namespace
sections.body: Pass the same namespace as the Vite configuration when this handler is imported directly from @kasperrt/smolter/utils/http rather than bundled by Vite. It selects the /path.__namespace data suffix and is validated like the Vite option. Export the compiled namespace from your SSR entry to keep both in one place.
